meta.phase-name: Gameplay Responsiveness And Content-Driven Board UX

phase-plan.purpose: Return the active development lane to the playable game. Improve responsiveness, room/entity readability, hover media, and board clarity while preserving the now-usable local authoring/import/publish path as a supporting tool rather than the current center of gravity.
phase-plan.scope: In scope: a dedicated turn-runner seam between KAPLAY UI and engine dispatch, a sync-then-dispatch worker contract for expensive turn resolution, explicit busy/pending state plus debug timing hooks in the UI, initiative/speed-aware queue evolution rooted in the existing engine meters, stronger room identity and entity visibility on the navigation board, simplified spellbook/menu flows, full-cell room iconography, sprite-driven room/entity portraits, actor-aware live-feed formatting, content-driven hover cards/media for rooms/hostiles/dungeoneers, and Playwright/unit/perf coverage for the core playable loop. Also in scope: updating gameplay-facing planning references so design and implementation stay aligned during the human feedback loop. Out of scope: broad new editor productization, generalized planner work in docs-site, and content-pipeline polish that does not directly improve playing or iterating on the game right now.

file.description: Current scene/runtime bootstrap and main-thread action execution. This is the first place to insert a dedicated turn runner and pending-turn UI state.
Bridge between KAPLAY and the engine package. It should stop being a direct synchronous dispatch surface and become the deterministic execution boundary for workerized or queued turn computation.

Main gameplay scene orchestration. It should consume pending-turn state, improve board readability, replace the combat-room fallback with room-focus scene tabs for treasure/training/rune forge, and stop embedding heavy turn work directly in input handlers.
Board rendering and retained decoration update path. This is the right place to improve room/entity marker readability without bloating the orchestration file again.
Pure mapping for room-feature icon language and special tile affordances like boss and exit rooms. Keep gameplay-facing icon choices deterministic and testable here.
Static icon sprite loader for the KAPLAY canvas. Use this to keep menu/room/board iconography consistent without dragging React UI dependencies into the standalone game.
Formats gameplay and livestream events into the player-facing feed. Keep the actor-aware MMO-style prefix language stable here so board iteration and review builds share the same event vocabulary.
Derived room visuals/cache keys. Use this layer to keep content-driven room identity and board diffing cheap.
Deterministic synchronous rules engine. Keep the game logic deterministic here even if execution moves behind a worker or queued turn runner on the UI side.
Current initiative-meter queue for autonomous actors. Use this as the basis for speed-aware queue planning instead of inventing a second scheduling model in docs.
Playwright smoke coverage for the playable game loop should grow here so gameplay regressions are visible without manual spelunking.
Turn-budget regression harness for the playable loop. Use it to keep worker/busy-state work honest with concrete average, p95, and max turn timings.
Primary gameplay design reference that should stay aligned with the room board, encounters, visibility, and content-authored presentation improvements.

task.description: Introduce a dedicated turn-runner seam in KAPLAY so gameplay input no longer assumes same-tick synchronous engine mutation. Keep the engine deterministic, but move the UI toward queued/background turn execution with explicit pending-state handling.

Improve room/entity readability on the board and HUD: stronger room identity, clearer hostile/dungeoneer presence, better same-room encounter emphasis, and hover/preview detail that makes location and occupancy obvious.
Bind the first content-driven media/icon previews into room/entity hover cards so authored content can drive the board language instead of placeholder text alone.
Add Playwright game smoke coverage for the navigation loop, room preview/selection, encounter visibility, and busy-turn behavior so the feedback loop stays fast and reviewable.

Lock explicit performance and queue targets around the playable loop: document the current turn-budget thresholds, keep initiative-meter ordering visible in status/debug output, and treat sprite/readability work as part of the same measured loop instead of disconnected polish.

Collapse combat-specific room presentation into the encounter path and introduce room-focus navigation scenes for treasure, training, and rune forge with concrete room actions plus keycap/icon-driven affordances.

Tighten the bag and spellbook overlay UX with icon-first filter/sort tabs, top-pinned context actions, clearer arrow-selection guidance, stronger selected-card borders, and rarity-driven visual treatment across items and spells.

Replace the bottom navigation panel with a player-facing live gameplay feed, standardize room/navigation keycaps around `M`, `R`, `V`, `X`, and `Space`, and remove ghost footer/action-slot clutter from room-focus scenes.

Close the treasure/dialogue/readability follow-up: treasure-room search should stay reward-first, dialogue/cutscene continuation must always return to movable navigation, header controls should render with keycap-style hints, and the live shell text needs a stronger readability pass.

Audit the live playable shell against the gameplay design and current content packs, then turn the resulting gaps into explicit phase tasks covering menu input contract drift, bag/item semantics drift, missing content visuals, and maintainability/perf follow-up.

Replace remaining cursor-like selection affordances and placeholder control copy in display/loadout overlays with command-board rows that show the actual keycap next to the action label; remove duplicate detail headers and unnecessary top borders while fixing menu text overflow.

Normalize bag/equipment taxonomy so normal inventory does not expose merchant-only sell flow, non-equipment treasure containers do not read like carried items, and weapons/equipment/consumables are visually distinguishable through consistent icon/sprite treatment.

Close the visible surfaced-content coverage gap by resolving generated/runtime item ids back to canonical sprites, using shared placeholder/icon fallbacks for gear and spell surfaces, and keeping currently surfaced gameplay content out of thin text-only rendering when authored art is missing.

Implement the gameplay-design livestream model as a persistent toggle/stateful mode and continue reducing overlay/list redraw churn so responsiveness work improves architecture and maintenance along with perceived speed.

decision.summary: Off-main-thread execution should not make the core engine semantically async. The engine remains deterministic and synchronous internally; the UI/runtime boundary becomes asynchronous.
decision.impact: This protects reproducibility, keeps tests simpler, and lets workerization improve responsiveness without rewriting gameplay rules around promises.

decision.summary: The active lane is gameplay-first again. Asset Explorer and local authoring remain supporting tools, but they are no longer allowed to eclipse readable, responsive play.
decision.impact: Implementation order now follows the human feedback loop in the game itself: play, observe, adjust, then return to content authoring when that loop needs better data/tools.

decision.summary: Room feature should drive the whole navigation shell, not just the tile color. The active room now owns the scene background and shell palette so combat, dialogue, forge, treasure, and rest spaces read differently at a glance.
decision.impact: This gives us a granular but global token model for future content/media polish and keeps room identity legible without requiring more HUD text.

decision.summary: Playable-loop smoke tests should assert structured board/debug state instead of relying only on screenshots or brittle text scraping.
decision.impact: The game now exposes board snapshots and turn timing events for Playwright, which makes gameplay iteration reviewable while we keep moving UI and performance targets.

decision.summary: Discovered rooms should read as a board game cell, not a tiny badge. The tile gets the room-driven fill, a large centered icon, and the room panel gets a sprite or icon portrait so the player recognizes space and occupants immediately.
decision.impact: This keeps the board scannable during movement, supports future authored media previews, and lets room/entity identity carry more of the UI load than raw text labels.

decision.summary: The turn worker should sync a snapshot once, then accept action-only dispatch requests until the state changes again. Do not ship the full snapshot payload on every player action if the worker is already synced.
decision.impact: This keeps the UI boundary asynchronous without making the engine async, reduces per-turn payload churn, and gives us a clean place to record timing/debug events around queueing, resolve, reject, and failure paths.

decision.summary: Speed-queue work should extend the existing initiative-meter model instead of replacing it with a second scheduler. Agility-driven gain, readiness thresholding, and ordered ready actors are now the active queue contract for autonomous runtime work.
decision.impact: This keeps queue behavior deterministic, lets performance work measure real queue cost instead of a fake placeholder, and gives UI/debug surfaces one stable queue story to expose while workers move heavy resolution off the main thread.

decision.summary: Boss rooms should stay visibly revealed on the board even before entry. The crown/exit affordance takes precedence over generic room-type iconography, and boss presence can read like a discovered piece before the player walks into the room.
decision.impact: This supports navigation planning, makes the floor objective obvious, and lets the board feel intentional instead of hiding the most important room behind the same discovery rule as filler spaces.

decision.summary: Room/board sprite language should use one shared priority order: boss, then hostile, then dungeoneer, then room emblem. The board marker, hover preview, and portrait panel should all resolve from the same presence summary and fallback order.
decision.impact: This avoids contradictory identity across views, keeps small sprites readable, and lets future authored media slot into one deterministic presentation pipeline instead of bespoke panel logic.

decision.summary: Movement should resolve as one turn, not silently chain an extra search turn. Search stays available as an explicit room action so the player understands why time advanced.
decision.impact: This removes a major source of perceived input lag, makes turn timing legible, and leaves room for a future initiative or speed-based queue without burying side effects inside a move.

decision.summary: Combat is encounter-driven, not room-feature-driven. Treasure, training, and rune forge should swap the navigation board into a focused room scene with concrete room actions, while hostile encounters remain the only combat-specific scene transition.
decision.impact: This removes contradictory room taxonomy, lets treasure/training/forge spaces feel authored instead of generic grid nodes, and keeps navigation, encounters, and room interaction on one coherent shell model.

decision.summary: The spellbook should own one clear preparation model: prepared slots on the left, unlocked spell pool in the center, codex only when relevant, and portrait-style detail on the right. Do not duplicate the same concept behind both a loadout label and a prepared-spells panel.
decision.impact: This cuts menu noise, makes slot assignment understandable, and gives us a cleaner surface for future content/media-driven spell presentation.

decision.summary: Gameplay and livestream events should share one actor-aware feed language with clear prefixes such as system, you, boss, dungeoneer, and live.
decision.impact: This gives Playwright and human review a stable event surface, makes dungeon activity skimmable, and turns the feed into part of the readability pass instead of debug leftovers.

decision.summary: The playable-loop perf harness is now a working guardrail, not an optional script. Keep average turn resolution at or below `700ms`, p95 at or below `1200ms`, and max at or below `1600ms` for the deterministic move-run sample unless the thresholds are intentionally re-baselined.
decision.impact: This gives “performance” a concrete meaning in the active phase, keeps queue/sprite work tied to measured cost, and prevents regressions from hiding behind qualitative “still feels laggy” reports alone.

decision.summary: True responsiveness work goes beyond workers. Initiative/speed-aware turn ordering is now part of the runtime direction, and the next deeper systems pass should extend that queue model plus background computation instead of falling back to blocking same-phase resolution.
decision.impact: We can remove the worst UI stalls now, but the lasting fix is to keep actor readiness explicit, preserve deterministic ordering, and keep more turn work off the main interaction path.

decision.summary: Bag and spellbook overlays should expose selection-specific actions at the top of the menu, not on a detached footer. Filter/sort tabs stay icon-first, arrow-selection hints stay visible, and rarity cues participate in the same readability pass as slot and sprite work.
decision.impact: This makes preparation and equipment flow legible at a glance, reduces footer hunting during keyboard or mouse use, and keeps menu clarity aligned with the broader board/readability work in the active gameplay phase.

decision.summary: The bottom navigation panel should serve the player-facing live feed, not a second room-action footer. Room focus already owns room detail in the center view; the footer should reinforce gameplay events and clear `M`/`R`/`V`/`X`/`Space` inputs instead of repeating room or move hints.
decision.impact: This keeps the shell focused on skimmable gameplay information, removes dead/ghost button surfaces, and aligns the navigation view with the MMO-style event feed direction in the gameplay design.

decision.summary: Treasure-room search should feel like a payoff, not a fake-out. Direct `search` keeps the loot message front and center, the disappointing locked-cache beat belongs to authored dialogue choices instead of the basic treasure-room search action, and dialogue continuation should drop the player back into navigation once the line resolves.
decision.impact: This keeps treasure rooms rewarding in the core loop, prevents the player from getting trapped in a stale overlay after a dialogue/cutscene beat, and makes the shared navigation shell easier to read by expressing controls as consistent keycap legends instead of bracketed text.

decision.summary: Menu and command surfaces should show the actual keyboard affordance beside the action row instead of leaning on cursor-like highlight frames, fake selector copy, or labels such as `change filter` that do not match the real input model.
decision.impact: This keeps menu language aligned with the navigation shell, makes keyboard use self-documenting, and removes the remaining debug-form/control-field feel from bag, map, and room overlays.

decision.summary: The normal bag/inventory overlay is not a shop screen. Merchant-only actions like `Sell` do not belong in the default bag command strip, and carried loot presentation should prioritize player-facing item identity rather than exposing internal or transitional item ids.
decision.impact: This reduces option noise, keeps equipment and consumables readable during normal play, and prevents inventory UX from leaking engine/economy implementation details into the player-facing shell.

decision.summary: Weapons, equipment, consumables, rooms, runes, rarities, titles, and gear slots should all resolve through one consistent icon/sprite/placeholder language. Text-only fallback remains acceptable for incomplete packs, but the playable shell should actively close those gaps instead of normalizing missing art as the steady state.
decision.impact: This makes loot and loadout surfaces scannable, keeps room/detail panels from collapsing into dense text blocks, and ties content growth to visible gameplay readability rather than leaving media coverage as optional polish.

decision.summary: The gameplay design defines livestreaming as a persistent on/off mode that drains mana and grants Fame over time, not a one-shot social action. Phase-64 parity work should implement that stateful contract rather than leaving livestream as a button that only loosely resembles the design.
decision.impact: This aligns the live runtime with the design doc, clarifies future feed/Fame/deed work, and prevents more UI polish from accruing around the wrong underlying gameplay contract.
